test_title: SSC MTS 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 08 Oct, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Find the simple interest (in ₹) on ₹4000 as a sum borrowed at 3% per year rate of interest for 6 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Effective rate of interest for 6 years = 3% × 6 = 18%

Simple Interest = 18% of Principal

⇒ Simple Interest = (18 ÷ 100) × 4000

⇒ Simple Interest = 18 × 40 = 720

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal (P) = ₹4000

Rate (R) = 3% p.a.

Time (T) = 6 years

**Formula Used:**

Simple Interest (I) = (P × R × T) ÷ 100

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/b3ac1942a675c734a86294696e061dd3e1da7e6431b7b669a06569a4de233ddb.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ I = (4000 × 3 × 6) ÷ 100

⇒ I = 40 × 18

⇒ I = 720

**∴ The correct answer is ₹720.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Total Amount Formula

The final amount after adding simple interest is given by A = P + I, which can also be written directly as A = P(1 + RT ÷ 100).

Simple vs Compound Interest

For the first year (when compounded annually), Simple Interest and Compound Interest are identical. From the second year onwards, Compound Interest is greater than Simple Interest for the same rate.

Time to Double Investment

Under Simple Interest, a sum of money doubles itself when the earned interest equals the principal. This always happens in Time = 100 ÷ R years.
